cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Hand It Over
cards.instruction: Persuade someone to give up control of a task, object, or decision you believe is being mishandled.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll handle the seating plan from here. Putting the exes together is asking for trouble.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're civil now. I checked with both of them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good groundwork. We'll keep your guest list and just separate their tables. Let me have the pencil.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I spent hours balancing those tables. You're not starting again.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One swap, then. You choose who trades seats with him, and I'll make the correction. Still your plan; I'm just keeping it running smoothly. Pencil?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 claims takeover authority; A3 credits B preparation and A5 limits the correction to B chosen swap to get the pencil.

relationship.evidence: B2 has actual social information and B4 protects a worked arrangement, so A must persuade rather than simply seize.

heightening.evidence: A5 reduces whole-plan takeover to one controlled edit while still seeking the decision instrument.

specificity.evidence: A1 exes seating and B4 balanced tables make the practical dispute understandable.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 final Pencil is an economical return to the concrete pursuit.
